leo: Quick async check — Q2 OKR milestone 'model-pipeline-stability'. Post one-liner: shipped / slipped / blocker / next action + owner. Ping folks you need @here :wave:

anna: Shipped: canary deploy completed for model v2-quant. Owner: anna. Notes: perf looks good, latency +3ms avg. :thumbsup:

sam: Slipped: autoscale policy integration for Dedicated pools. Owner: sam. Blocker: infra RPC schema mismatch that's blocking the rollout. ETA: aiming for EOD Thu if shim lands.

maria: Blocked: private deployment e2e failing on KV cache with long sequences. Owner: maria. Error snippet: ```ERROR KVCache: OOM when allocating 6.2GB``` Trying temp mitigation: lower batch_size (BATCH=4) to unblock tests.

jin: SRE note: saw p95 tail increase on canary ~02:14 UTC, possibly correlated with memory allocations during streaming. I'll pull traces and linked logs. Owner: jin.

leo: For the autoscale RPC: @sam who in eng-infra should we loop in? @jin can you paste the trace once you have it so we can correlate?

sam: Looping in @maya (eng-infra) — maya can you look at the RPC shim? @maria let's try the reduced batch tonight and see if tests pass.

maya: On it. I'll add a compatibility shim for the RPC this morning. ETA PR by 3pm PT. Will post link in this thread when ready.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-17T10:12Z started by anna — model v2-quant — status: in-progress

anna: If canary goes green we'll promote at 16:00 PT. If memory spike persists we'll hold and rollback to v1.

maria: Quick workaround update: patched e2e harness to set BATCH=4, rerunning full suite now. If green I'll open a follow-up to root-cause and schedule a fix for KV sizing.

jin: Trace link: https://internal.logs/trace/abc123 — p95 spike correlates with KVCache allocations. Adding to incident timeline and tagging owners.

leo: Next actions recap: sam/maya -> finish RPC shim PR; maria -> confirm e2e with BATCH=4; jin -> confirm trace correlation + add timeline. Post quick status updates here, we won't block ship calls unless failing. Thanks all.
